topic_tag: a town's ditch-clearing duty over two centuries
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: By 1900, one historian observes, the ditch rule had become ______.

worlds.passage: In 1712 a market town ordered every household to send one adult each spring to spend two days clearing the town's drainage ditches, or else to pay a fine of one shilling. In the 1850s the council laid covered brick drains beneath the streets to carry the water that had run in those open channels. The rule was never repealed and still stands in the town's printed code, the clerk's muster book has no entries after 1858, and the town's 1890 street plan shows rows of houses along the lines the channels once followed. By 1900, one historian observes, the ditch rule had become ______.
worlds.explanation: Brick drains took over the ditches' work, houses now stand where the channels ran, and no muster has been held since 1858, so the rule, though never repealed, had become "obsolete." "Onerous" fails because no one was being made to do the work at all. "Profitable" fails because with no muster there was no fine to collect. "Porous" fails because the rule was not riddled with exemptions; it simply had nothing left to apply to.

onerous.quote: the clerk's muster book has no entries after 1858
onerous.why: no one was being summoned, so the rule burdened no one

profitable.quote: rows of houses along the lines the channels once followed
profitable.why: with the channels built over and no muster held, no one owed work or fine, so the rule brought in nothing

porous.quote: covered brick drains beneath the streets
porous.why: the rule lapsed because its object disappeared, not because exemptions let people slip through it

worlds.passage: In 1712 a market town ordered every household to send one adult each spring to spend two days clearing the town's drainage ditches, or else to pay a fine of one shilling. As the town spread along the valley, its ditches lengthened from two miles to eleven, while the number of households grew far more slowly. The council raised the duty from two days to nine and the fine from one shilling to ten, and in the 1890s the court heard a steady stream of laborers who could neither spare the days nor pay. By 1900, one historian observes, the ditch rule had become ______.
worlds.explanation: The ditches grew far faster than the number of households sharing the work, so the duty rose to nine days and the fine to ten shillings, more than laborers could bear; the rule had become "onerous." "Obsolete" fails because the ditches still existed and still had to be cleared. "Profitable" fails because the people summoned could not pay the fine. "Porous" fails because no one is described as excused; the burden fell on every household.

obsolete.quote: its ditches lengthened from two miles to eleven
obsolete.why: the ditches still existed and grew, so the rule still applied to something

profitable.quote: could neither spare the days nor pay
profitable.why: people could not pay the fine, so the rule brought in no money

porous.quote: the number of households grew far more slowly
porous.why: the work was spread over every household, with no group excused, which is why each share grew

worlds.passage: In 1712 a market town ordered every household to send one adult each spring to spend two days clearing the town's drainage ditches, or else to pay a fine of one shilling. The fine stayed at one shilling while wages rose, and by the 1850s a shilling was less than half of what a laborer earned in a day. By the 1880s the clerk's books show a shilling from nearly every household each spring, and the council paid hired crews to clear the ditches for a fraction of that sum. By 1900, one historian observes, the ditch rule had become ______.
worlds.explanation: As wages rose the fixed fine became cheaper than a day's work, nearly every household paid it, and the council cleared the ditches for a fraction of the takings, so the rule had become "profitable" for the town. "Obsolete" fails because the ditches still had to be cleared and the rule still paid for that. "Onerous" fails because the fine had become a small sum. "Porous" fails because the rule still collected from nearly every household; no one was excused.

obsolete.quote: paid hired crews to clear the ditches
obsolete.why: the ditches still needed clearing, and the rule's fines still paid for it

onerous.quote: less than half of what a laborer earned in a day
onerous.why: the fine had shrunk in real terms, so the rule weighed lightly

porous.quote: a shilling from nearly every household
porous.why: the rule still reached nearly every household; no group had been let out of it

worlds.passage: In 1712 a market town ordered every household to send one adult each spring to spend two days clearing the town's drainage ditches, or else to pay a fine of one shilling. Over the next century the council excused, one group at a time, members of the militia, shopkeepers on market days, anyone who kept a horse for hire, and anyone past fifty. By the 1890s the clerk's spring muster, still called every year, drew fewer than one household in five, and the clerk's books show the ditches only partly cleared in most springs. By 1900, one historian observes, the ditch rule had become ______.
worlds.explanation: Exemption after exemption let four households in five slip out of a duty that was still called every spring, and the work stopped getting done; the rule had become "porous." "Obsolete" fails because the muster was still held for ditches that still needed clearing. "Onerous" fails because the remaining households did not take on the extra work; the ditches were simply left half-cleared. "Profitable" fails because the excused owed neither work nor fine.

obsolete.why: the rule was still being applied each spring to ditches that still needed clearing

onerous.quote: the ditches only partly cleared in most springs
onerous.why: the remaining households were not made to cover the others' share; the work was left undone

profitable.quote: the council excused, one group at a time
profitable.why: excused households owed neither work nor fine, so the rule yielded less, not more
